title: Verification query contract v0.1
description: FTC §4.4 'portability by contract': a verification query is declared with a dialect and an expected result shape; an evaluator is conformant iff it executes the dialect and checks the returned rows against the shape. Two documents validate here: (a) a resolved query object {dialect, text, expected_shape} — what the engine evaluates, whether it came from the descriptor's own `verification_query` / `dialect` / `expected_shape` fields (flow.spec/v0.2) or from a binding; (b) a query-binding file (apiVersion flowtrace.queries/v0.1) that binds (flow, step, scenario) to such an object, used when the descriptor carries a natural-language placeholder (`<...>`) or a dialect the adapter does not execute. See spec/coverage-engine.md §5.

dialect.description: Query language, e.g. otel-sql (the reference adapter), promql, traceql, datadog. Adapters declare the dialects they execute.

min_rows.description: The result must have at least this many rows.

required_columns.description: Every name must be a column of the result (order-insensitive).

text.description: The query in that dialect. A text of the form `<...>` is a placeholder (natural-language intent), never executed.

stream.description: Revision 2026-10-11 (FTC §4.4; spec §4.1): the stream the query reads. A scenario that needs a required attribute of class content reads the sampled stream; everything else the assurance stream. When absent the engine decides from the scenario's required_data (free text, so a heuristic); declaring it here is the contract.
